expertInsight: Salesforce now calls Pardot Marketing Cloud Account Engagement. The product name changed in 2022. Salesforce’s current credential name is Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Specialist; “Pardot Specialist” remains a useful legacy search term.

personas.label: Marketing coordinators and specialists

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Account Engagement Specialist Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Account Engagement Specialist exam checks whether you can use the product’s main marketing features. Study prospect records, administration, forms, lead management, email, and Engagement Studio. Be ready to apply settings to practical tasks.
bullets: Format: The guide lists 60 scored multiple-choice or multiple-select questions, up to five unscored questions, and 90 minutes.
72% to pass, which is 44 correct answers out of 60.
Exam topics: The guide covers visitors and prospects, administration, forms and landing pages, lead management, email marketing, and Engagement Studio.
Preparation: Practice the product tasks in a safe account and check your study against the current official exam guide.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use the exam outline as a checklist. Practice setting up forms, lists, scoring, automation, and nurture programs, then explain what each setting will do to a prospect record.

examFormat.heading: Account Engagement Specialist Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center and uses multiple-choice and multiple-select questions.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Salesforce does not publish the share of scenario questions. Prepare to apply the product features to tasks involving prospects, forms, email, automation, and Salesforce sync.
bestWayToPass: Choose the right automation: Know what happens after one asset interaction, what an ongoing rule evaluates, and how a nurture program guides prospects over time.
Separate interest from fit: Scoring reflects prospect activity. Grading reflects how well a prospect matches the target profile.
Follow prospect sync: Learn how prospects connect to Salesforce leads and contacts, how field sync settings work, and what access the connector user needs.
Practice forms and profiling: Know when a form handler fits an existing external form, and how progressive profiling gathers new details over repeat visits.

differentiation.heading: Account Engagement Specialist Traps & Readiness Checklist
differentiation.intro: Review the exact behavior of Account Engagement features as well as the marketing concepts behind them.

commonTraps.trap: Assuming every automation tool does the same job
commonTraps.fix: Choose completion actions for a response to an asset interaction, automation rules for ongoing criteria, and Engagement Studio for timed journeys with branches.
A score reflects engagement; a grade reflects profile fit. Use both when deciding how sales should follow up.
Check field synchronization settings and connector permissions, including which system’s value wins when fields differ.

commonTraps.trap: Choosing Pardot Forms when a Form Handler is required
commonTraps.fix: Use a Pardot Form for hosted capture and progressive profiling. A Form Handler connects an existing external form.

readinessBenchmarks: You can distinguish dynamic, segmentation, and suppression lists from automation rules.
You have built an Engagement Studio program with waits, rules, and completion actions.
You can investigate a prospect sync issue using field values, ownership, and connector access.
You can explain the official objectives and why each practice answer fits.
whoShouldSkip: You have not yet configured Account Engagement assets or its Salesforce connector.
Your work centers on Journey Builder, Automation Studio, or Email Studio; consider Email Specialist first.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests hands-on configuration of Account Engagement (Pardot) -- automation rules, scoring and grading, forms, Engagement Studio programs, email sends, and Salesforce connector sync. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 72% pass mark, weighted towards Lead Management (24%) and Account Engagement Forms, Form Handlers and Landing Pages (20%).
topics: Account Engagement Forms, Form Handlers and Landing Pages (20%)

blocks.heading: Scoring and grading
blocks.body: Scoring estimates interest based on actions such as form submissions, email clicks, and page visits. Grading measures fit with a target profile, using details such as role, industry, or company size. A prospect may show strong interest but still be a poor fit. Use both measures to support lead qualification.

blocks.heading: Automation tools
blocks.body: Completion actions run after a prospect interacts with a specific asset. Automation Rules evaluate prospects against criteria and can take actions when the criteria match. Engagement Studio guides prospects through a nurture program with waits, rules, triggers, and actions. Segmentation Rules create a list from criteria at the time the rule runs; Dynamic Lists update as prospects meet or stop meeting criteria.

blocks.heading: Salesforce sync
blocks.body: Account Engagement and Salesforce can hold values for the same field. Its sync behavior setting decides how differences are handled, such as Salesforce taking precedence, Account Engagement taking precedence, or the most recently updated value winning. Check the connector user’s access when records or fields do not sync as expected.

blocks.heading: Visitors and prospects
blocks.body: A visitor is not yet identified. When a person submits a form or follows a tracked email link, Account Engagement may associate browser activity with a prospect record. Dynamic Lists update membership based on current criteria. Scoring Categories keep separate scores for different products or areas of interest.

blocks.heading: Forms and form handlers
blocks.body: An Account Engagement form is hosted by the product and supports features such as validation and progressive profiling. A form handler connects an existing external form to Account Engagement. Choose based on whether the client can replace the form and which form features the process needs.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Specialist Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Specialist exam focuses on using Account Engagement features correctly. Work through the task the marketer needs to complete, then pick the feature that handles it.

blocks.heading: Lists and automation
blocks.body: Use Dynamic Lists for groups that should update as prospect data changes. Use a Segmentation Rule for a group fixed at the time it runs. Match Completion Actions, Automation Rules, and Engagement Studio to the event or journey.

blocks.heading: Email and deliverability
blocks.body: Check the sending setup and domain authentication when delivery is poor. Learn the purpose of SPF and DKIM, and use appropriate recipient lists and consent settings.

blocks.heading: Dynamic content
blocks.body: Dynamic content changes a section of an asset based on prospect data. Define a default version and test each variation so every recipient sees suitable content.

blocks.heading: Forms and progressive profiling
blocks.body: Use a form handler when an external form must remain in place. Progressive profiling can request new fields on later visits. Check which follow-up actions run after submission.

blocks.heading: Salesforce sync
blocks.body: When data does not appear as expected, check the connector user’s access, the field sync behavior, and the prospect’s related Salesforce record.

sampleQuestions.question: A person who has not been identified submits an Account Engagement form. What happens next?
options: Account Engagement creates a prospect record using the submitted identifying details
The person remains a visitor until a sales rep creates a Salesforce lead
The form submission starts every active Engagement Studio program
Salesforce creates a contact, but Account Engagement keeps no record
sampleQuestions.explanation: A visitor becomes a prospect once identified by email address, which the form submission supplies. Account Engagement can then associate the captured activity with that prospect.
whyWrong: A sales rep does not need to create the prospect manually after an identified form submission.
A form submission does not enroll someone in every running program.
Account Engagement records the prospect as well as the form activity.

sampleQuestions.question: Which action usually adds to a prospect’s score?
options: Working for a company in the target industry
Holding a job title listed in the ideal customer profile
Working at a company of the preferred size
Opening a marketing email and clicking a link
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scoring reflects engagement activities such as email opens and link clicks. Grading uses profile attributes to measure fit.
whyWrong: Industry is a profile detail used to assess fit.
Job title is a profile detail used to assess fit.
Company size is a profile detail used to assess fit.

sampleQuestions.question: A prospect downloads several guides but works at a company outside the target market. How should the record reflect this?
options: Low score and high grade
High score and high grade
High score and low grade
Low score and low grade
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scoring measures how interested a prospect is, and the downloads show interest. Grading measures fit, so this prospect should have a lower grade.
whyWrong: The downloads show activity, so the score should not be low.
A poor fit should not receive a high grade simply for being active.
The prospect is engaged, so the score should be high.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to keep its existing website form and capture the submissions in Account Engagement. Which feature should it use?
options: An Account Engagement landing page linked from the site
A form handler connected to the external form
A Dynamic List populated from the site database
An Account Engagement form that replaces the external form
sampleQuestions.explanation: Form handlers connect Account Engagement to existing external forms, so the client can keep its form design and send submissions to the product.
whyWrong: A landing page does not capture submissions from the form the company wants to keep.
A Dynamic List groups prospects; it does not receive form submissions.
Replacing the form would not meet the requirement to keep the existing form.

sampleQuestions.question: The team needs to apply a field update to prospects across the database whenever they meet a changing set of criteria. Which tool should they use?
options: An Automation Rule
A Completion Action on a landing page
A static list made by a Segmentation Rule
A one-time export from Salesforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: Automation Rules continually check updated prospects against criteria and can run again when Repeat Rule is enabled. This lets the rule apply actions when prospects meet the criteria again.
whyWrong: A Completion Action runs after a specific asset interaction.
A Segmentation Rule creates a list at the time it runs.
A one-time export does not continue to evaluate changing criteria.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketer wants a fixed list of prospects who met criteria when a campaign launched. What should they run?
options: A Dynamic List
A Completion Action
A Segmentation Rule
An Engagement Studio trigger
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Segmentation Rule creates a list based on the criteria at the time it runs.
whyWrong: A Dynamic List changes as prospects meet or stop meeting its criteria.
A Completion Action responds to an asset interaction.
A trigger checks for behavior within a nurture program.

sampleQuestions.question: A lead is deleted in Salesforce, but its Account Engagement prospect record remains. What should the admin expect?
options: The connector pauses until an admin approves the deletion
The Salesforce deletion does not automatically delete the prospect record
Account Engagement creates a replacement lead in Salesforce
The prospect is removed from all Account Engagement lists immediately
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Salesforce lead deletion does not automatically remove the associated prospect record from Account Engagement.
whyWrong: A deletion does not necessarily pause the connector.
The deletion does not itself create a replacement lead.
The prospect record can remain until separately handled.

sampleQuestions.question: Salesforce and Account Engagement contain different values for a synced field. What determines which value is kept?
options: The system with the most custom fields
The field’s sync behavior setting
The system where the record was first created
The user who most recently viewed the record
sampleQuestions.explanation: The sync behavior configured for that field determines how conflicting values are handled.
whyWrong: The number of custom fields does not decide which value wins.
Record creation order is not the field sync setting.
Viewing a record does not change its field value or sync precedence.

sampleQuestions.question: A prospect clicks a tracked link in an email and then browses the company website. Why can Account Engagement connect that activity to the prospect?
options: The tracked link ties the browser to a known prospect
The website automatically creates a Salesforce contact for every visitor
The prospect’s company IP address identifies the individual
A tracking cookie identifies every visitor before they click the email
sampleQuestions.explanation: A tracked email link can associate the browser with a known prospect, so later visits can be added to that record.
whyWrong: A website visit does not automatically create a contact.
A shared company IP address does not reliably identify an individual.
Before identification, a tracking cookie alone does not tell the system who the person is.

sampleQuestions.question: Marketing emails are reaching spam folders. Which setup should the team review first?
options: Whether prospect grades are included in the email template
Whether Engagement Studio has a wait step before each message
Check SPF and DKIM for the sending domain
Whether Dynamic Lists are sorted by score
sampleQuestions.explanation: SPF and DKIM help mail systems confirm that the sending domain is authorized to send the message.
whyWrong: Grades in a template do not authenticate the sender.
Wait steps control timing, not domain authentication.
List sorting does not authenticate email.

sampleQuestions.question: A new Salesforce field is not syncing to Account Engagement. What should the admin check?
options: Whether the prospect has opened an email recently
Whether the connector user has access to the object and field
Whether the prospect is on a Dynamic List
Whether the field is included in an Engagement Studio program
sampleQuestions.explanation: The connector user needs suitable access for the object and field to sync.
whyWrong: Email activity does not grant field access.
Dynamic List membership does not control field permissions.
A program does not enable field synchronization.

sampleQuestions.question: A returning prospect should see only the form fields not already collected. Which feature supports this?
options: A completion action
A scoring category
A form handler
Progressive profiling
sampleQuestions.explanation: Progressive profiling can present new fields on later visits instead of asking for the same details again.
whyWrong: A Completion Action runs after an asset interaction.
A Scoring Category separates scores; it does not control form fields.
A Form Handler connects an external form to Account Engagement.

sampleQuestions.question: A prospect should wait three days before moving to the next step in Engagement Studio. Which element creates the delay?
options: A wait step
A trigger
A rule
An action
sampleQuestions.explanation: A wait step holds the prospect for the set period before the program continues.
whyWrong: A trigger checks for behavior.
A rule checks prospect data.
An action performs a task; it does not create a time delay.

sampleQuestions.question: Within Engagement Studio, what does a trigger check that a rule does not?
options: Whether prospect data matches set criteria
Whether the prospect has reached a score threshold
Whether the prospect has performed a behavior such as clicking an email
Whether the prospect belongs to a particular Salesforce campaign
sampleQuestions.explanation: A trigger waits for a prospect action, such as an email click. A rule checks information already stored on the prospect.
whyWrong: Checking stored prospect details is the role of a rule.
A score threshold is a data condition a rule can evaluate.
Campaign membership is prospect data, not a behavior trigger.

sampleQuestions.question: A prospect submits a form and should receive a follow-up action tied only to that form. Which feature fits?
options: A Dynamic List based on the prospect’s current score
A Segmentation Rule that runs once each morning
An Automation Rule that watches the entire prospect database
A Completion Action on the form
sampleQuestions.explanation: Completion Actions run after a prospect interacts with a specific asset, such as submitting this form.
whyWrong: A Dynamic List updates membership but does not run a one-time form-specific follow-up.
A Segmentation Rule creates a list from criteria at the time it runs.
An Automation Rule evaluates prospect criteria, rather than responding only to this form submission.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketer wants one email to show different product information based on each prospect’s industry. What should they add?
options: A Segmentation Rule
A Form Handler
A separate email send for every prospect
Dynamic Content
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dynamic Content can show different sections of an asset based on prospect field values.
whyWrong: A Segmentation Rule groups prospects but does not vary content within an email.
A Form Handler receives data from an external form.
The same asset can serve different content without sending a separate email to each person.

introLead.text: This guide covers hands-on Marketing Cloud Account Engagement work: prospects, lists, lead qualification, forms, email, automation, and Salesforce sync. The 16 sample questions focus on day-to-day setup and troubleshooting. Compare your study plan with Salesforce’s
